'''Petra Deimer''' (9 March 1948, in [[Göttingen]] – 27 March 2024<ref>[https://trauer.shz.de/traueranzeige/petra-deimer-schuette-2024 Obituary], 6. April 2024. Retrieved 11 December 2024 (in German).</ref>) was a German [[Marine biology|marine biologist]], and [[Conservation (ethic)|nature conservationist]] who has been actively involved in the study and protection of [[marine mammals]], particularly [[cetacea]]ns, since the mid-1970s.

==Career==
Deimer gained her PhD in marine biology, with a particular focus on [[sperm whale]]s, at the [[University of Hamburg]].<ref>[http://www.madeira-news.de/reportagen/umweltschutz/81-petra-deimer-und-ihre-wale Petra Deimer and her whales] (in German)</ref> In the late 1970s many species of whale, including sperm whales, were in danger of extinction.<ref>Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora, Mar. 6 1973, 27 U.S.T. 1087, 993 U.N.T.S. 243</ref> As a result of Deimer's actions, the [[archipelago]] of [[Madeira]] was declared a protection zone for marine mammals, and commercial whaling around Madeira ceased in 1981.<ref name="gsm">[http://gsm-ev.de/en/2001/04/05/golden-ark-for-the-marine-biologist-petra-deimer/ Golden Ark for the Marine Biologist, Petra Deimer] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180502140317/http://gsm-ev.de/en/2001/04/05/golden-ark-for-the-marine-biologist-petra-deimer/ |date=2 May 2018 }}, gsm-ev.de. Accessed 1 June 2024.</ref>

She contributed significantly to the decision of the [[International Whaling Commission]] (IWC) to ban commercial whaling in July 1982.<ref>International Whaling Commission Schedule, para. 10(e).</ref> In 1983 Deimer ensured that the trade in Minke whales was also banned.<ref>C. Epstein, ''The Power of Words in International Relations: Birth of an Anti-Whaling Discourse'' (Cambridge, Mass, 2008), p. 159.</ref>

Deimer is the founder and president of the Society for the Conservation of Marine Mammals (Gesellschaft zum Schutz der Meeressäugetiere; GSM).<ref>[http://gsm-ev.de/en/2003/09/05/hanse-environmental-award-2003/ Hanse] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180502141047/http://gsm-ev.de/en/2003/09/05/hanse-environmental-award-2003/ |date=2 May 2018 }}, GSM-ev.de. Accessed 1 June 2024.</ref> She is a member of the International Whaling Commission's (IWC) Scientific Committee, a member of the German government's Species Conservation Advisory Committee, and an advisor to the [[International Fund for Animal Welfare]] (IFAW).<ref name="gsm" />

<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://gsm-ev.de/en/2001/04/05/golden-ark-for-the-marine-biologist-petra-deimer/ |title=Golden Ark for the Marine Biologist, Petra Deimer |access-date=2 May 2018 |archive-date=2 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180502140317/http://gsm-ev.de/en/2001/04/05/golden-ark-for-the-marine-biologist-petra-deimer/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2001, Deimer was awarded the [[Order of the Golden Ark|Golden Ark]] for nature conservation by [[Prince Bernhard of Lippe-Biesterfeld|Prince Bernhard of the Netherlands]].<ref name="gsm" />

Deimer has written six books, and numerous articles on whales, dolphins, and seals, as well as on environmental conservation more generally. She has also written a book on parrots.{{citation needed|date=June 2024}}

==Select Bibliography==
*''Whales and Dolphins'' (1998) (English translation of: ''Wale und Delphine'')
*''Parrots: A complete pet owner’s manual'' (1984) (trans. Rita Kimber) (English translation of: ''Papageien'')
*''Das Buch der Wale'' (Hamburg, 1983) (''The Book of Whales'')
*''Das Buch der Robben'' (Hamburg, 1987) (''The Book of Seals'')
